_comment: Tauri binary integrity manifest. Mirrors the structure of voice_typer/server/native/binaries.json but for the Tauri host binary (voice-typer-tauri) that the autostart launcher spawns at login. (2026-10): each binary entry's `sha256` field is now a per-(platform, arch) dict (e.g. `{"linux-x86_64": "...", "linux-aarch64": "..."}`) so the manifest can disambiguate the same binary file name across architectures. macOS uses the single key `macos` because the .app bundle ships a universal Mach-O binary (x86_64 + arm64 slices). The legacy flat-string `sha256` field is replaced by this dict — the loader (verify_tauri_binary_or_skip, to be added to autostart_launcher.py) MUST consult the per-arch sub-key matching `platform.system().lower()` + '-' + `platform.machine()` (with macOS collapsed to `macos`). At runtime, the proposed verify_tauri_binary_or_skip(path) helper hashes the discovered binary with hashlib.sha256 and compares against the per-arch sha256 here. On mismatch (or missing/empty manifest entry for the running platform/arch), the helper logs an error and the autostart launcher falls back to spawning the Electron dev binary instead of an untrusted Tauri binary. Entries with an empty sha256 (binaries not built in this Linux dev tree) cause verify_tauri_binary_or_skip to FAIL CLOSED (return False + log ERROR) — production builds MUST populate all per-arch sha256 fields via scripts/build/update_tauri_manifests.py, run by CI after each platform's Tauri build (record mode hashes the built binary into this manifest; --check enforces non-empty hashes, fail-closed on release builds). The _install_paths arrays are ORDER-SENSITIVE and pinned to the autostart launcher's discovery order (voice_typer/server/autostart_launcher.py::_TAURI_LAUNCHER_INSTALL_PATHS) by tests/tauri/test_config_script_drift.py::TestLauncherInstallPathsMatchManifest — Windows lists the per-user NSIS currentUser target (LOCALAPPDATA) first because the launcher checks it before the admin PROGRAMFILES path. The min_proto_version field is reserved for future IPC protocol-version gating (PVT-G5-063 follow-up); the loader does not yet enforce it. VT_TAURI_BINARY env-var override: when set, the autostart launcher uses that path UNCHANGED — the proposed verify_tauri_binary_or_skip(path) call MUST still verify it against this manifest so an attacker cannot use VT_TAURI_BINARY to bypass the integrity gate (the env var is the documented attack vector).

voice-typer-tauri.app._note: The macOS bundle name is APP_NAME (Voice Typer); the inner executable is the Cargo binary name (voice-typer-tauri). The sha256 is computed over the inner executable, NOT the .app bundle. macOS ships a universal Mach-O binary (x86_64 + arm64 slices) so the manifest uses a single `macos` key rather than separate `macos-x86_64` / `macos-aarch64` keys.

_schema_changelog: v1 (2026-09): flat `sha256: "<hex>"` string per binary entry. v2 (2026-10): `sha256` is now a per-(platform, arch) dict so the manifest can disambiguate the same binary file name across architectures. The loader (verify_tauri_binary_or_skip) MUST consult the per-arch sub-key matching the running platform/arch rather than the flat string.
_manifest_loader_contract: The loader (verify_tauri_binary_or_skip, to be implemented in autostart_launcher.py) MUST: (1) look up the binary by Path.name (matching one of the keys in 'binaries'); (2) read the per-(platform, arch) sha256 dict — compute the lookup key as `<platform>-<arch>` where platform is platform.system().lower() (with 'darwin' collapsed to 'macos') and arch is platform.machine().lower() (with 'amd64' normalized to 'x86_64'); for macOS the key is just 'macos' (universal binary); (3) if the sub-key is missing OR the value is empty OR the entry is missing, FAIL CLOSED (log ERROR, return False) — production builds must populate every per-arch sub-key; (4) if the sub-key has a non-empty value, compute hashlib.sha256(path.read_bytes()).hexdigest() and compare with hmac.compare_digest against the expected value; (5) on mismatch, log ERROR and return False. The loader MUST NOT silently trust a binary whose manifest entry is missing or has an empty per-arch sha256 (CR-002 fail-closed semantics, mirroring voice_typer/server/native_hotkeys/binary_path.py:517-562). The default (bare) values of the sha256 dicts are EMPTY and must never be committed to a release — scripts/build/update_tauri_manifests.py --check exits non-zero on any empty sub-key.
_updater_contract: scripts/build/update_tauri_manifests.py is the ONLY writer of the per-arch sha256 fields. It maps a Rust target triple to a manifest key via TRIPLE_TO_MANIFEST_KEY (same mapping as tests/tauri/test_config_script_drift.py TRIPLE_TO_MANIFEST_KEY — drift-pinned), hashes the cargo-built binary (linux/windows: <target-dir>/<triple>/release/voice-typer-tauri[.exe]; macos: the inner executable of the <triple>/release/bundle/macos/<productName>.app bundle), and writes only the matching key(s), leaving all other entries untouched. --check re-validates the whole manifest (every non-macos sub-key must be a 64-char lowercase hex string; macOS 'macos' must be non-empty) and exits 1 otherwise.
